title: G Thang and Leon Haywood
hook: G Thang is a 1975 Leon Haywood slow jam.
voiceover: G Thang is a 1975 Leon Haywood slow jam. Leon Haywood, born in Houston, working out of Los Angeles. In 1975 he put out I Want'a Do Something Freaky to You on 20th Century Records. It's a bedroom record, and the intro is that bass line and the guitar sting every head knows. In 1992 Dr. Dre took that intro, kept it close to the original tempo, and built Nuthin' but a G Thang on top of it for The Chronic. Snoop's first verse sits right where Leon's vocal used to. The flip isn't a chop. It's a lift, with new drums and that whining synth on top. Save this, then go pull the Haywood and hear how much Dre kept.
caption: Nuthin' but a G Thang (Dr. Dre and Snoop, The Chronic, Death Row, 1992) is built on the intro of I Want'a Do Something Freaky to You by Leon Haywood (20th Century, 1975). Dre barely chopped it. He lifted the groove, added drums and the synth lead, and let Snoop sit where Leon's vocal used to be. The best flips are sometimes the least clever ones. Which West Coast flip next? ☀️
cover_text: G Thang is a 1975 slow jam
